Format ANOVA tables in APA style

Source: R/anova.R
apa_anova.Rd

Makes an analysis of variance source table with sums of squares, degrees of freedom, mean squares, F tests, p-values, and effect sizes. Values come from parameters::model_parameters(), and effect sizes come from the effectsize package (e.g., effectsize::eta_squared()).

Usage

apa_anova(
  fit,
  anova_parameters = c("Parameter", "Sum_Squares", "df", "Mean_Square", "F", "p",
    "Effect_Size"),
  effect_size = c("eta", "omega", "epsilon"),
  partial = TRUE,
  generalized = FALSE,
  type = NULL,
  ci = 0.95,
  residual_label = "Error",
  starred = NA,
  bolded = NA,
  column_formats = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'lm'
apa_anova(
  fit,
  anova_parameters = c("Parameter", "Sum_Squares", "df", "Mean_Square", "F", "p",
    "Effect_Size"),
  effect_size = c("eta", "omega", "epsilon"),
  partial = TRUE,
  generalized = FALSE,
  type = NULL,
  ci = 0.95,
  residual_label = "Error",
  starred = NA,
  bolded = NA,
  column_formats = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'aovlist'
apa_anova(
  fit,
  anova_parameters = c("Parameter", "Sum_Squares", "df", "Mean_Square", "F", "p",
    "Effect_Size"),
  effect_size = c("eta", "omega", "epsilon"),
  partial = TRUE,
  generalized = FALSE,
  type = NULL,
  ci = 0.95,
  residual_label = "Error",
  starred = NA,
  bolded = NA,
  column_formats = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'anova'
apa_anova(
  fit,
  anova_parameters = c("Parameter", "Sum_Squares", "df", "Mean_Square", "F", "p",
    "Effect_Size"),
  effect_size = c("eta", "omega", "epsilon"),
  partial = TRUE,
  generalized = FALSE,
  type = NULL,
  ci = 0.95,
  residual_label = "Error",
  starred = NA,
  bolded = NA,
  column_formats = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'afex_aov'
apa_anova(
  fit,
  anova_parameters = c("Parameter", "df", "df_error", "Mean_Square", "F", "p",
    "Effect_Size"),
  effect_size = c("eta", "omega", "epsilon"),
  partial = TRUE,
  generalized = TRUE,
  type = NULL,
  ci = 0.95,
  residual_label = "Error",
  starred = NA,
  bolded = NA,
  column_formats = NULL,
  ...
)

# Default S3 method
apa_anova(fit, ...)

Arguments

fit

an aov or lm model, a repeated-measures aov model with an Error() term (class aovlist), an afex model (class afex_aov), or an ANOVA table from stats::anova() or car::Anova().

anova_parameters

columns to display. "Effect_Size" stands for whichever effect size effect_size, partial, and generalized select, and "CI" adds its confidence interval as [LL, UL]. Columns not in the ANOVA table are silently dropped.

effect_size

effect size to display: "eta" (\(\eta^2\), default), "omega" (\(\omega^2\)), or "epsilon" (\(\epsilon^2\)). If NULL, no effect size is computed.

partial

if TRUE (default), partial effect sizes (e.g., \(\eta^2_p\)) are displayed. For one-way designs, partial and non-partial effect sizes are the same.

generalized

if TRUE, generalized \(\eta^2\) (\(\eta^2_G\)) is displayed instead, which is comparable across between- and within-subjects designs. Only for effect_size = "eta".

type

type of sums of squares for aov and lm models: 1 (sequential, default, as in stats::anova()), 2, or 3. Types 2 and 3 are computed with car::Anova(). Type 3 tests are interpretable only when factors have sum-to-zero contrasts (e.g., contr.sum) and covariates are centered. Ignored for ANOVA tables, which already have a type.

ci

confidence level for the effect size interval, shown if anova_parameters includes "CI". Intervals are two-sided, so a 90% interval excludes 0 when the F test is significant at \(\alpha\) = .05, and its lower bound is 0 otherwise. Intervals are not shown for generalized \(\eta^2\), because those computed by effectsize can exclude the point estimate.

residual_label

label for residual (error) rows

starred

columns to star with significant p-values (e.g., "F")

bolded

columns to bold, if significant

column_formats

column_formats object to format columns. If NULL, the default column_formats is used.

...

further arguments passed to parameters::model_parameters()

Value

apa7_tbl (tibble)

Details

For repeated-measures models fit with aov(y ~ a * b + Error(id / b)), each error stratum is introduced by a heading row ("Between subjects" or "Within subjects"), and each stratum's error term follows its effects.

Model comparisons (e.g., anova(m1, m2)) are not ANOVA source tables. Use apa_performance_comparison() for them.

For afex models (afex::aov_car(), afex::aov_ez(), afex::aov_4()), each effect has its own error term, so the table shows each effect's degrees of freedom (df~effect~, df~error~), mean squared error (MSE), F, p, and effect size, as in afex's own nice() tables. Degrees of freedom and p-values reflect the sphericity correction set in afex (Greenhouse-Geisser by default), and generalized \(\eta^2\) is the default effect size, as in afex.

Examples

d <- mtcars
d$cyl <- factor(d$cyl)
d$am <- factor(d$am)
fit <- aov(mpg ~ cyl * am, data = d)
apa_anova(fit)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   Source   `*SS*` `*df*` `*MS*` `*F*`   `*p*`   `*&eta;*^2^~p~`
#>   <chr>    <chr>  <chr>  <chr>  <chr>   <chr>   <chr>          
#> 1 Cyl      824.78  2     412.39 "44.85" "<.001" ".78"          
#> 2 Am        36.77  1      36.77 " 4.00" " .06 " ".13"          
#> 3 Cyl × Am  25.44  2      12.72 " 1.38" " .27 " ".10"          
#> 4 Error    239.06 26       9.19 ""      ""      ""             

# Omega squared with a 90% confidence interval
apa_anova(
  fit,
  anova_parameters = c(
    "Parameter", "Sum_Squares", "df", "Mean_Square", "F", "p",
    "Effect_Size", "CI"
  ),
  effect_size = "omega",
  ci = .90
)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 8
#>   Source   `*SS*` `*df*` `*MS*` `*F*`   `*p*`   `*&omega;*^2^~p~` `90% CI`    
#>   <chr>    <chr>  <chr>  <chr>  <chr>   <chr>   <chr>             <chr>       
#> 1 Cyl      824.78  2     412.39 "44.85" "<.001" ".73"             "[.56, .82]"
#> 2 Am        36.77  1      36.77 " 4.00" " .06 " ".09"             "[.00, .29]"
#> 3 Cyl × Am  25.44  2      12.72 " 1.38" " .27 " ".02"             "[.00, .13]"
#> 4 Error    239.06 26       9.19 ""      ""      ""                ""          

# Type 2 sums of squares (requires the car package)
if (requireNamespace("car", quietly = TRUE)) {
  apa_anova(fit, type = 2)
}
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   Source   `*SS*` `*df*` `*MS*` `*F*`   `*p*`   `*&eta;*^2^~p~`
#>   <chr>    <chr>  <chr>  <chr>  <chr>   <chr>   <chr>          
#> 1 Cyl      456.40  2     228.20 "24.82" "<.001" ".66"          
#> 2 Am        36.77  1      36.77 " 4.00" " .06 " ".13"          
#> 3 Cyl × Am  25.44  2      12.72 " 1.38" " .27 " ".10"          
#> 4 Error    239.06 26       9.19 ""      ""      ""             
if (requireNamespace("afex", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(obk.long, package = "afex")
  fit_afex <- afex::aov_ez(
    "id", "value", obk.long,
    between = "treatment", within = "phase", fun_aggregate = mean
  )
  apa_anova(fit_afex)
}
#> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'lme4':
#>   method           from
#>   na.action.merMod car 
#> Contrasts set to contr.sum for the following variables: treatment
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   Effect        `*df*~effect~` `*df*~error~` `*MSE*` `*F*` `*p*` `*&eta;*^2^~G~`
#>   <chr>         <chr>          <chr>         <chr>   <chr> <chr> <chr>          
#> 1 Treatment     2.00           13.00         6.41     2.91  .09  .27            
#> 2 Phase         1.74           22.64         0.81    19.29 <.001 .21            
#> 3 Treatment × … 3.48           22.64         0.81     5.43  .004 .13
